title: Doubling Machine
brief: Build a reusable machine you can call again and again. Your Doubling Machine takes a number, doubles it, and hands the answer back with return.

problem.goal: Finish the double() function so that it returns its number multiplied by 2, and the program prints the doubled answer.
rules: The function must return the answer, not print it.
The doubling happens inside the function, not in the code below it.
The function has to work for any number typed in, not just one.
Leave the input line and the print line as they are.

steps: Look at the function double(number). Right now its body is just pass, so it does nothing and hands nothing back.
Replace the pass line with return number * 2.
The bottom part is already written: it asks for a number, calls your function, and prints what came back.
Press Run and try a number, then press Check project.
starterCode:
# 🔢 Doubling Machine: give it a number and it hands back double!

# 1) Finish this function so it RETURNS the number times 2:
def double(number):
    pass    # replace this line

# This part asks for a number and uses your function:
n = int(input("Give me a number to double: "))
answer = double(n)
print("Doubled:", answer)
hints: Run the code before changing anything. It prints Doubled: None, because a function whose body is just pass hands nothing back, and nothing is None.
The line you need is return number * 2, indented four spaces so it sits inside the function.
Use number, not n. Inside the function, the value you were given is called number. That is the whole point of a parameter: the function does not need to know what the caller named it.
If you write print(number * 2) instead of return, the answer appears on screen but answer still holds None, so the last line prints Doubled: None underneath it.
Do not do the doubling on the last line. The function is supposed to be the machine, so print("Doubled:", answer) should stay exactly as it is.
inputHint: Type one number for the machine to double.
successMessage: Boom! You built a real function that takes a number in and returns an answer, then reused it on any number. That is exactly how programmers avoid writing the same code twice.
